stories.title: Attackers Exploit UnrealIRCd Flaw That Enables Server-Level Command Injection
stories.abstract: CISA has added eight vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, including a critical command injection flaw in UnrealIRCd and various issues affecting Cisco, Microsoft, Google, and Barracuda products, all of which are currently being leveraged by threat actors in the wild.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are actively exploited in the wild, posing a significant risk of unauthorized access, remote code execution, or system compromise.
stories.action: Review CISA KEV catalog and apply all available security patches for the listed affected software immediately.

stories.title: Check Point security advisory (AV26-1154) – Update 1
stories.abstract: Check Point has disclosed two vulnerabilities affecting its firewalls, management servers, and orchestration platforms. One of these flaws, CVE-2026-123039, is currently being actively exploited in the wild and has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
stories.why: Active exploitation of perimeter security infrastructure poses a critical risk to network integrity and administrative access control.
stories.action: Review Check Point advisory AV26-1154 and apply all available security patches immediately.

stories.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808
stories.abstract: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices are vulnerable to critical remote code execution flaws, collectively dubbed php2shell, stemming from the underlying PHP runtime. These vulnerabilities allow unauthenticated attackers to potentially execute arbitrary code on affected industrial hardware.
stories.why: These flaws carry a 9.8 CVSS score and are actively exploited, posing a severe risk to critical infrastructure and industrial control systems.
stories.action: Restrict network access to affected devices and implement vendor-recommended security configurations immediately.

stories.title: Siemens Desigo, Gridscale
stories.abstract: A critical out-of-bounds write vulnerability, dubbed Node2Shell, affects the Brotli decoder in various Siemens industrial products, including Desigo, Gridscale, and RUGGEDCOM. Exploitation could allow remote attackers to corrupt memory or execute arbitrary code on vulnerable systems.
stories.why: This flaw carries a 9.8 CVSS score and impacts critical infrastructure, posing a significant risk of remote code execution in industrial environments.
stories.action: Update Siemens Desigo, Gridscale, and RUGGEDCOM software to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Cisco BroadWorks and Openwave Flaws Actively Exploited Despite Available Patches
stories.abstract: CISA has added multiple vulnerabilities affecting Cisco BroadWorks, Cisco Crosswork, and various Barracuda products to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog. These flaws are currently being leveraged in active cyberattacks, necessitating immediate attention from administrators managing these enterprise infrastructure components.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities are confirmed to be under active exploitation, significantly increasing the risk of unauthorized access or system compromise.
stories.action: Update Cisco and Barracuda products to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: Google security advisory (AV26-1157)
stories.abstract: Google has released security updates for Chrome to address a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-125350, which is currently being exploited in the wild. The flaw affects Windows, Mac, and Linux versions of the browser.
stories.why: This vulnerability is actively exploited by threat actors, making it a high-priority risk for all enterprise and personal browser environments.
stories.action: Update Chrome to version 157.0.8103.78 or later immediately.

stories.title: Exploit Attempts for GPUStack Authentication Bypass (CVE-2026-102895), (Thu, Nov 12th)
stories.abstract: A critical authentication bypass vulnerability in GPUStack, tracked as CVE-2026-102895, allows unauthorized access to GPU cluster management systems. The flaw affects all versions released before 2.2.0 and is currently seeing active exploitation attempts in the wild.
stories.why: GPUStack manages high-value AI infrastructure; unauthorized access grants attackers control over expensive compute resources and sensitive machine learning workloads.
stories.action: Update GPUStack to version 2.2.0 or later immediately.

stories.title: SCKit Malware Turns ScreenConnect Support Sessions Into Potential MSP Attack Paths
stories.abstract: Attackers are leveraging a critical vulnerability in ConnectWise ScreenConnect to deploy the SCKit malware. This campaign targets remote access sessions, allowing unauthorized actors to establish persistent control over managed service provider environments through previously identified security gaps.
stories.why: Exploitation of remote management tools provides adversaries with high-privilege access to downstream client networks, facilitating widespread supply chain compromise.
stories.action: Ensure all ScreenConnect instances are updated to the latest patched version.

stories.title: Uber drivers' information stolen in a third-party hack
stories.abstract: Uber notified drivers that their personal information, including driver's license details, was compromised following a security breach at Fireworks AI, a third-party cloud provider used by the ridesharing company.
stories.why: Third-party vendor breaches remain a significant supply chain risk, exposing sensitive employee and contractor data even when internal systems remain secure.

stories.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
stories.abstract: A researcher released a proof-of-concept exploit dubbed SignDrop that allows local users to escalate privileges to System-level access on Windows systems. The vulnerability stems from how the operating system handles signature verification, potentially enabling unauthorized administrative control.
stories.why: Local privilege escalation flaws are critical for attackers who have already gained a foothold on a machine and need to bypass security boundaries.

stories.title: Check Point warns of zero-day flaw exploited for root access
stories.abstract: Check Point has issued emergency patches for a critical vulnerability affecting its Security Gateway products. Attackers have been actively exploiting this flaw since late October to escalate privileges to root level and maintain persistent access within compromised network environments.
stories.why: The vulnerability allows unauthenticated attackers to gain full control over security appliances, facilitating lateral movement and long-term network espionage.
stories.action: Apply the emergency hotfixes provided by Check Point immediately.

stories.title: Hackers Exploit PHP2Shell Flaws in Check Point Gateways to Deploy TSGA Backdoor and Wipe ESXi Files
stories.abstract: Threat actors are exploiting unpatched Check Point Security Gateways to gain initial access via PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. Attackers then leverage a local privilege escalation flaw in the Gaia OS to install a backdoor and deploy data-wiping malware targeting VMware ESXi environments.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates a sophisticated pivot from network edge appliances to hypervisor-level destruction, posing a severe risk to virtualized infrastructure and data integrity.
stories.action: Patch Check Point Security Gateways immediately and audit Gaia OS configurations for unauthorized access.

stories.title: SilentAir Hijacks Asian Telecom Networks to Intercept SMS 2FA Codes and Spy on Taiwanese Users
stories.abstract: A state-sponsored threat actor dubbed SilentAir has compromised telecommunications infrastructure across six Asian nations. By infiltrating mobile network nodes, the group successfully intercepted SMS messages and voice calls, specifically targeting individuals within Taiwan.
stories.why: This highlights critical vulnerabilities in telecom supply chains and the ability of sophisticated actors to bypass standard encryption by compromising core network equipment.

stories.title: Craft CMS security advisory (AV26-1086) - Update 1
stories.abstract: Craft CMS has released security updates to address multiple vulnerabilities, including CVE-2026-123488, which is currently being exploited in the wild. Affected versions include CMS versions prior to 4.18.9 and 5.11.2, as well as the Commerce-mollie plugin prior to 4.4.3.
stories.why: Active exploitation of a CMS vulnerability poses a significant risk of unauthorized access or remote code execution on web infrastructure.
stories.action: Update Craft CMS to 4.18.9 or 5.11.2 and Commerce-mollie to 4.4.3 immediately.

stories.title: N-able security advisory (AV26-1143)
stories.abstract: N-able has addressed a critical vulnerability, CVE-2026-125883, affecting its N-central platform. Reports indicate this security flaw is currently being exploited in the wild. Administrators must ensure their environments are running version 2026.4.1.26 or later to mitigate potential unauthorized access.
stories.why: Active exploitation of remote management software poses a significant risk for supply chain attacks and lateral movement within managed networks.
stories.action: Update N-central to version 2026.4.1.26 or higher immediately.

stories.title: FBI Says North Korean Hackers Stole Over $400 Million in Crypto Using Deepfake Video Calls
stories.abstract: The U.S. government has dismantled a North Korean social engineering operation known as FaceStealer. Over the past year and a half, the campaign successfully targeted victims to siphon more than $400 million in cryptocurrency assets.
stories.why: It highlights the sophisticated use of social engineering by state-sponsored actors to facilitate large-scale financial theft and money laundering.

stories.title: Citrix Patches 12 NetScaler and Secure Access Client Flaws, Including Authentication Bypass
stories.abstract: Citrix has released security updates addressing ten critical vulnerabilities across NetScaler ADC, Gateway, and Console products. These flaws include a high-severity memory overflow issue and other bugs that could allow remote attackers to trigger denial-of-service conditions or bypass authentication mechanisms.
stories.why: NetScaler appliances are high-value targets for initial access; unpatched vulnerabilities in these edge devices frequently lead to full network compromise.
stories.action: Update NetScaler ADC, Gateway, and Console to the latest patched versions immediately.

stories.title: New N-able "4EverAble2Shell" zero-day exploited hours after PoC released
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively exploiting a zero-day vulnerability in N-able N-central, identified as 4EverAble2Shell. The flaw allows unauthorized server compromise and has been leveraged to install cryptocurrency miners on at least 21 systems, including those already running the most recent security patches.
stories.why: This highlights the rapid weaponization of proof-of-concept code and the failure of existing patches to mitigate the specific attack vector.

stories.title: Operation Endgame Takes Down Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC Servers, Seizes 6.4M Stolen Logins
stories.abstract: International law enforcement agencies executed Operation Endgame, dismantling infrastructure supporting Gootloader, CastleRAT, and StealC malware. The operation seized over 230 servers and 250 domains, while recovering more than 6.4 million stolen credentials linked to widespread ransomware and data theft campaigns.
stories.why: This disruption significantly degrades the operational capacity of major malware-as-a-service providers frequently used for initial access and credential harvesting.

stories.title: n8n security advisory (AV26-1160)
stories.abstract: The Canadian Cyber Centre issued advisories for three distinct products: n8n workflow automation software, Apache HTTP Server, and Johnson Controls EasyIO firmware. Each platform contains security vulnerabilities requiring administrative attention to mitigate potential exploitation risks.
stories.why: These updates address critical flaws, including an OAuth account hijacking vulnerability in n8n and potential remote code execution vectors in Apache.
stories.action: Update n8n to 3.0.1+, Apache HTTP Server to 2.4.71, and patch Johnson Controls EasyIO firmware.

stories.title: No Signs of Hacking in FAA Ground Stop as FBI Reportedly Probes Software Update
stories.abstract: Federal authorities have found no evidence of a cyberattack following a nationwide FAA ground stop. Preliminary investigations suggest the disruption was likely triggered by a faulty software update rather than malicious activity.
stories.why: Systemic failures in critical infrastructure often trigger security concerns, necessitating verification that outages are operational rather than the result of unauthorized access.

stories.title: Citrix security advisory (AV26-1150)
stories.abstract: Citrix released security updates addressing 28 memory-related vulnerabilities across NetScaler ADC, Gateway, and Console products, as well as Secure Access Clients for Linux and Windows. One flaw, CVE-2026-120868, impacts all deployments and can cause denial of service or unpredictable system behavior.
stories.why: Unpatched NetScaler appliances are frequent targets for exploitation; these memory flaws could lead to service disruption or potential remote code execution.
stories.action: Update NetScaler ADC, Gateway, Console, and Secure Access clients to the latest vendor-specified versions immediately.

stories.title: New SignDrop Zero-Day Exploit Turns Windows CLFS Security Feature Into SYSTEM Access
stories.abstract: A new proof-of-concept exploit dubbed SignDrop targets the Windows Common Log File System driver. By manipulating path redirection during log-authentication processes, local attackers can escalate privileges to SYSTEM level, bypassing security controls introduced in recent driver updates.
stories.why: This vulnerability allows local privilege escalation, enabling attackers to gain full administrative control over compromised Windows systems.

stories.title: PostgreSQL Patches 52 Flaws, Including 22-Year-Old Bug Enabling Authenticated RCE
stories.abstract: PostgreSQL released updates addressing 52 vulnerabilities, most notably a critical type confusion flaw, CVE-2026-6460. This 22-year-old bug allows authenticated users with object-creation privileges to execute arbitrary code on the underlying server with the database process's system-level permissions.
stories.why: Authenticated attackers can achieve full remote code execution, bypassing standard database restrictions to compromise the host operating system.
stories.action: Update PostgreSQL and rebuild all installed C-language extensions.

stories.title: Beware the New AI-Fueled Ransomware Boom
stories.abstract: While fully autonomous ransomware remains theoretical, threat actors are increasingly leveraging generative AI to lower the barrier to entry. These tools allow less skilled individuals to execute more effective attacks, increasing the overall volume and sophistication of malicious campaigns.
stories.why: AI lowers the technical threshold for cybercriminals, potentially leading to a surge in ransomware frequency and more convincing social engineering tactics.

stories.title: PTC Patches Critical Windchill and FlexPLM Flaw That Could Enable Remote Code Execution
stories.abstract: Apache has released version 2.4.71 to address a critical remote code execution vulnerability in the mod_http2 module. The flaw, CVE-2026-119618, impacts servers running versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 that have HTTP/2 enabled, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary code.
stories.why: Remote code execution in a widely deployed web server poses a severe risk of full system compromise and lateral movement.
stories.action: Update Apache HTTP Server to version 2.4.71 immediately.

stories.title: Attacker Used 4,837 Hijacked GitHub Accounts to Run a CI Secret Stealer in 1,806+ Repositories
stories.abstract: Threat actors hijacked nearly 5,000 GitHub accounts to inject malicious code into thousands of repositories. The campaign, known as wfx-loot, uses automated pull requests to deploy credential-stealing malware designed to harvest sensitive cloud environment secrets and CI/CD workflow tokens.
stories.why: Compromised CI/CD pipelines provide attackers with direct access to production cloud infrastructure and sensitive environment variables.
stories.action: Audit repository pull requests and rotate all secrets or API keys exposed within CI/CD workflows.

stories.title: In Other News: New CISA Director Nominee, Connected Car Hacking, Baker Tilly Data Breach
stories.abstract: Microsoft researchers identified potential security risks involving backdoored AI model weights, while OpenAI faces scrutiny regarding vulnerabilities in its Codex model. Meanwhile, Siemens has updated its security advisory protocols, and recent reports highlight emerging threats to connected vehicles and significant corporate data breaches.
stories.why: AI supply chain integrity and model poisoning represent emerging attack vectors that could compromise downstream applications relying on third-party machine learning components.

stories.title: Cursor confirms security breach led to malicious Claude Code extension
stories.abstract: The AI code editor Cursor experienced a security breach after attackers compromised Fireworks AI credentials. This unauthorized access allowed threat actors to inject a malicious Claude Code extension into the Cursor marketplace, potentially exposing users who installed the compromised plugin.
stories.why: Supply chain attacks targeting developer tools can lead to widespread source code theft or the injection of backdoors into production environments.
stories.action: Review and remove any suspicious or recently installed extensions from your Cursor environment.

stories.title: Microsoft 365 Crawls Back to Life After a 24-Hour Outage
stories.abstract: Microsoft 365 services experienced a global outage lasting approximately 24 hours. The company confirmed the disruption stemmed from a faulty software update rather than malicious activity or artificial intelligence interference.
stories.why: Service reliability failures highlight the risks of automated deployment pipelines and the potential for widespread operational downtime caused by internal configuration errors.

stories.title: University of Texas at Arlington warns personal information stolen during cyberattack
stories.abstract: The University of Texas at Arlington confirmed that unauthorized actors accessed and exfiltrated personal data during a recent cyberattack. The institution has not disclosed the specific types of information compromised or the scale of the breach.
stories.why: Data breaches at academic institutions often expose sensitive PII, creating long-term identity theft risks for students, faculty, and staff.

stories.title: City of Osaka warns of data breach impacting 1 million as Japan reels from dozens of cyber incidents
stories.abstract: Osaka officials have alerted residents to potential phishing campaigns following a significant data breach. The city is warning its population to exercise caution regarding unsolicited emails that appear to originate from municipal authorities.
stories.why: Large-scale municipal data leaks often facilitate highly targeted social engineering and identity theft campaigns against residents.

stories.title: German military drone operations disrupted by cyberattack
stories.abstract: Quantum Systems, a German defense contractor, recently identified a cyberattack targeting its infrastructure. The company confirmed that hostile actors initiated the breach in late October, prompting an investigation into the scope of the intrusion and potential impact on drone operations.
stories.why: Compromised defense supply chains pose significant risks to national security and the integrity of sensitive military hardware.

stories.title: Trezor Confirms Hidden Implants in CryptoBilis-Sold Wallets That Can Steal Recovery Phrases
stories.abstract: Trezor discovered malicious hardware implants in three Safe 5 wallets sold by a Southeast Asian reseller. These unauthorized circuit boards capture recovery phrases displayed on the screen and transmit the data to attackers via cellular networks.
stories.why: Supply chain compromises of hardware wallets bypass standard security features, rendering physical device integrity untrustworthy if sourced from unauthorized third-party vendors.
stories.action: Purchase hardware wallets exclusively from the manufacturer or verified official partners.

stories.title: Macfinger ClickFix campaign sends DownTheDRAIN infostealer for macOS, (Fri, Nov 13th)
stories.abstract: The Macfinger ClickFix campaign is actively distributing the DownTheDRAIN infostealer targeting macOS users. This malicious operation utilizes deceptive prompts to trick victims into executing harmful payloads, potentially compromising sensitive system and user data.
stories.why: This campaign demonstrates evolving social engineering tactics specifically designed to bypass macOS security controls and exfiltrate credentials or private information.
